digest.intro: A thin day with one genuinely strange story, one infrastructure shock, and a few things worth making or thinking about.

items.title: Jensen Huang resigns amid board probe into employee relationships and suspected China ties
items.blurb: The HN thread surfaces the deeper story: a second relationship, a board investigation, and whispers about a Megaspeed connection — with Apple's Johny Srouji reportedly being eyed as successor. The end of an era for the most consequential chip company of the last decade.

items.title: Microsoft's global outage may be worse than CrowdStrike's
items.blurb: Governments, hospitals, and courts scrambled as Microsoft blamed failed server health checks. The scale is reportedly larger than the CrowdStrike incident — a reminder of how much critical infrastructure runs on a single vendor.

items.title: AI unlocks Gödel's notebooks, said to contain hundreds of proved theorems
items.blurb: Gödel worked in a private shorthand that defeated scholars for decades. AI transcription and reasoning apparently cracked it — and what's inside may reopen questions he never published. The kind of story that makes you think about what else is sitting in dead men's drawers.

items.title: The four forces that shape collective memory
items.blurb: Why we all remember Napoleon's name and forget almost everyone else who shaped his era. A framework for how memory propagates through culture — relevant if you think about mythmaking and lore.

items.title: Show HN: My $300 embroidery machine needed a subscription, so I built my own app
items.blurb: Classic maker rebellion: locked hardware, so someone built the whole software stack from scratch. The HN thread surfaces a small ecosystem of open embroidery tools worth knowing about if you ever want to stitch physical work.

items.title: Isometric SF: a pixel-art map built from Google's Photorealistic 3D Tiles
items.blurb: 1,300 square miles of the Bay Area converted into an isometric pixel-art rendering. The technical write-up is the real thing — a smart pipeline from 3D tiles to a view that feels handcrafted.

items.title: Brain implant trial volunteers want more autonomy and fewer NDAs
items.blurb: The people whose bodies host experimental neural hardware are pushing back on how research is structured — asking for agency over their own data and participation. A quiet but important shift in how we think about consent at the frontier of neuroscience.

art_picks.title: Sans Soleil
art_picks.creator: Chris Marker
art_picks.why: A meditation on memory, ritual, and the hidden systems by which cultures encode meaning into images — Marker treats documentary footage like a generative system, finding the deep structure under the surface of everyday life. Made in 1983, still the sharpest film about how images construct reality.

art_picks.title: Reassemblage
art_picks.creator: Visible Cloaks
art_picks.why: Spencer Doran and Ryan Carlile build music that sits exactly at the edge where physical and digital meet — acoustic instruments processed into something that feels like watching light refract through glass, beautiful on the surface with a rigorous generative architecture underneath.

art_picks.title: The Paintings for the Temple
art_picks.creator: Hilma af Klint
art_picks.why: A hidden system of symbols, sacred geometry, and cosmological feedback loops that af Klint worked on in obsessive secrecy for years — art that is literally a diagram of invisible forces, and one of the great examples of someone going unreasonably deep on one narrow thing.

events.name: Elmgreen & Dragset: TRANSITION
events.why: A 40-ton traversable corten-steel Oval Office you can walk through — architecture as power critique, physical environment as psychological experience; exactly the kind of obsessive, category-blurring installation that uses built space to make a system visible.

events.name: Gottlieb/Rothko: The Surrealist Years
events.why: A focused look at the moment two painters were actively constructing a new symbolic language — before Abstract Expressionism hardened into an institution, when the system was still being invented and the symbols still raw.

events.name: Nia Archives
events.why: Nia Archives is doing something genuinely interesting — using jungle and drum & bass (UK rave subculture, heavily coded with community and identity) as a vehicle for personal storytelling; a small-room show before she outgrows rooms like this.

events.name: Surprise Chef
events.why: Australian instrumental group treating vintage soul and library music as systems to be decomposed and rebuilt — deeply craft-focused, zero hype, and National Sawdust is one of the best-designed listening rooms in New York.

events.name: artport: A History of Internet Art
events.venue: Whitney Museum of American Art, 99 Gansevoort Street
events.why: 25 years of the Whitney's net art platform in one room — 100+ commissioned works from Golan Levin and Casey Reas to Morehshin Allahyari, with the gallery floor laid out like floating browser windows; this is the institutional history of the early internet as an artistic medium, made physical.
